title: Route-level latency atlas with stream-mode cohorting and adaptive bucketing
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build an interactive Route-level Latency Atlas that surfaces p50/p95/p99 by model and route with explicit streaming vs non-streaming cohorting and adaptive latency bucketing. The Atlas should make it fast for SREs, platform engineers, and PMs to identify regressions, link to traces, and understand whether regressions are tied to IO-mode (streaming/non-streaming), request shape, or model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard exposes p50/p95/p99 heatmap by model x route with time slider (1h/6h/24h/7d)
Toggle to split views: combined, streaming-only, non-streaming-only
Cohort explorer able to group by request_shape, sequence_length_bucket, and tenant; persistent URL for sharing
Top-100 slow requests table includes trace_id links that open the trace viewer and GitHub-friendly permalink
Anomaly rule created: p99 increase >25% for a route held for 10m triggers an incident notification channel
Query cost keeps within budgeted cardinality budget (max 12M series/day for observability pipeline)
Instrumented tracing hooks add 'route', 'model.family', 'model.version', and 'io_mode' tags to spans at request entry
implementation_notes: Metrics: use HDR histograms for latency buckets to preserve percentiles without heavy pre-aggregation; record p50/p95/p99 from histograms at query time
Tags: add io_mode=(streaming|nonstreaming) and request_shape=(short|medium|long) via request enricher in the edge proxy
Tracing: default sampling 1% for full flamegraphs, 100% for 'slow' traces where latency > p95 of route; attach trace_id to slow-metrics rows
Pipeline: update metrics/log pipeline to keep route+model+io_mode cardinality but drop ephemeral worker_id to avoid explosion
Storage: retention for histogram aggregates 90d; raw spans 14d; adjust cold-storage tier for 90-day SLO investigation
UI: use stacked heatmap + cohort table; expand row to show mini-sparklines for p50/p95/p99 over selected window
Cost tradeoff: implementing io_mode tag increases unique metric series ~3x for model-heavy routes; compensate with adaptive rollups for low-traffic tenants
decisions: Use HDR histograms instead of fixed bucket counters to limit series cardinality while allowing accurate percentile computation
Sample full traces at 1% cluster-wide, but override to 100% for any request classified as 'slow' (latency > route.p95) to ease debugging
Expose streaming split as a first-class toggle rather than separate dashboards to reduce context switching
Keep io_mode tag at metric layer but restrict additional high-cardinality tags (e.g., sandbox_id) behind a feature flag
risks_and_tradeoffs: Cardinality growth: adding model x route x io_mode increases series and query cost—mitigation: adaptive rollups and tenant-aware sampling
Latency computation load: computing percentiles from histograms at query-time increases query CPU—mitigation: scheduled pre-aggregates for high-traffic routes
Trace volume: raising slow-trace capture to 100% can flood tracing storage during global incidents—mitigation: cap per-tenant slow-traces/day and backpressure traces ingestion
UI complexity: too many cohort dimensions will confuse users—mitigation: ship with 3 default cohort dims and allow advanced multi-select
